recognize_zh: 三顆芽細胞核質比高、染色質細緻，下方芽細胞的細胞質中可見一條細長粉紅色的棒狀包涵體（Auer rod），直接指向骨髓性（myeloid）來源。
features: Medium to large blasts with high N:C ratio and round to slightly indented nuclei
Finely granular, open chromatin with faint nucleoli
Moderate pale blue cytoplasm; a slender pink-red Auer rod in the cytoplasm of the lower blast
Adjacent cell with dense purple-black granules obscuring the nucleus, most consistent with a basophil
Background erythrocytes with mild poikilocytosis and occasional crenated cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows circulating blasts with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, fine chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli and a moderate rim of pale basophilic cytoplasm. One blast contains a single slender Auer rod. A basophil is also present, and red cells show mild poikilocytosis. The presence of an Auer rod establishes myeloid lineage; findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia, with subclassification (e.g., AML with maturation) requiring marrow evaluation, flow cytometry and genetic studies.

ddx.vs: Lymphoblasts never contain Auer rods and are MPO negative, TdT and B- or T-lineage marker positive.
APL cells have bilobed nuclei with heavy granulation or multiple bundled Auer rods (faggot cells) rather than a single rod in an agranular blast.
Auer rods can occur in MDS, so blast percentage below 20% in blood and marrow and dysplasia define MDS rather than AML.
Döhle bodies are pale blue irregular cytoplasmic patches in maturing neutrophils, not needle-shaped pink rods in blasts.
